title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
claim: Prior flow methods treat time as an abstract denoising index; ours integrates a latent velocity field in physical time within a full architecture.
layout: 3 panels: two stacked contrast plots left, large architecture diagram right, left-to-right flow
description: The figure has three panels. On the left, (a) Flow matching and (b) Physical-time flow are stacked as small axis plots. Both have denoising time steps k on the vertical axis and physical time t on the horizontal axis. In (a), a vertical blue-to-red arrow runs from random noise at k=0 up to data samples at k=1, labeled with the velocity v_FM and x^1 = s_t. In (b), a thick horizontal blue arrow runs along physical time from latent state z_0 to z_T, labeled with v_θ(z_t, t; z_0, c) and z_t = f_dyn(s_t; s_0). On the right, (c) is a large block diagram of ODEWorld. An image sequence x_0…x_g goes through a frozen DINO encoder, then a dynamics encoder, then a latent velocity field box in teal. The velocity field feeds a dynamics decoder and a DINO decoder to give the reconstructed x̂_t. A dashed JVP first-order supervision branch sits at the bottom. Pastel blue, green, orange and teal blocks mark the different representation types.
caption: Illustration of PT-Flow and ODEWorld. (a), (b) Comparison between flow matching and our proposed PT-Flow. Although both methods learn time-dependent velocity fields and perform generation with ODE solvers, their notion of time and design philosophies are completely different. (c) Model architecture of ODEWorld.
abstract: In the physical world we inhabit, space and time are fundamentally continuous. However, existing machine learning paradigms for world modeling are largely confined to discrete-time prediction, thereby exhibiting significant inefficiency in capturing the dynamics of physical world. We introduce Physical-Time Flow (PT-Flow), a novel approach that learns a continuous latent velocity field operating in physical time. Crucially, the underlying dynamics of sequential data are parameterized by an ordinary differential equation (ODE) embedded in a well-structured representation space. Under this paradigm, the prediction of future can be recast as temporal integration via an ODE solver in the compressed latent space. Building upon PT-Flow, we construct ODEWorld, a continuous-time latent world model that is both efficient and versatile. By extracting time-variant features and enforcing ODE properties on both the dynamical representation space and the latent velocity field, ODEWorld effectively addresses the long-standing representation collapse issue in latent world model literature. This also enables high-quality image reconstruction even after long-horizon prediction. Moreover, its continuous nature allows for arbitrary temporal resolution and even backward prediction, which is impossible for most discrete-time models. Lastly, ODEWorld can provide rich planning-oriented information to facilitate downstream policy learning. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that ODEWorld successfully reconciles planning-conducive dynamics abstraction with visual realism, excelling in both video generation and robotic control. Project page: https://dstate.github.io/odeworld_website/.
